definitions.full: H2487. chaliphah [ חֲלִיפָה ] noun feminine a change (from idea of replacing, changing, substituting , compare Arabic, Aramaic) — suffix חֲלִיפָתִי Job 14:14 ; plural absolute חֲלִיפוֺת Judg 14:19 3 t.; construct id. 14:13 ; 2Kin 5:5 ; חֲלִפוֺת Gen 45:22 2 t.; חֲלִפֹת 45:22 ; Judg 14:12 ; — 1 change of raiment ׳ח שׂמלת Gen 45:22 (twice in verse), elsewhere ׳ח בגדים Judg 14:12-13 , 2Kin 5:5 , 22 , 23 ; so without בגדים Judg 14:19 . 2 relays 1 Kings 5:28; compare ׳ח וצבא Job 10:17 (Di). 3 revival after death , under figure of relief from military service Job 14:14 . 4 changing, varying , of course of life לָ֑מוֺ חֲלִיפוֺת אֵין אֲשֶׁר Psa 55:20 of the wicked, with whom are no changings , i.e. they do evil incessantly, steadily (|| אלהים יָרְאוּ ולא ) so Kmp Hu De Sch and others; but the expression is peculiar and obscure; Calv vicissitudes ; Hengst discharges ; text perhaps corrupt.

occurrences.englishText: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.

Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle now. If you can tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing;
but if you can’t tell me the answer, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.”

Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of them. He took their plunder, then gave the changes of clothing to those who declared the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.
The king of Syria said, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.”

He said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, even now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent† A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds of silver and two changes of clothing.’ ”

Naaman said, “Be pleased to take two talents.” He urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and laid them on two of his servants; and they carried them before him.
You renew your witnesses against me,
If a man dies, will he live again?
He raises his hands against his friends.
